questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: PPH is the most common cause of maternal mortality in India. Match the blood-loss definition – after vaginal delivery : after C-section : ACOG (any delivery).
questions.exp: PPH ≥500 mL after vaginal delivery, ≥1000 mL after C-section; ACOG ≥1000 mL after any delivery. (Book p528)

questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three clinical definitions of PPH?
opts: Excessive bleeding after delivery requiring blood transfusion
Blood loss with signs and symptoms of hypovolemia
Fall in hematocrit by ≥10% between admission and postpartum period
questions.exp: Clinical definitions: need for transfusion, hypovolemic signs, ≥10% hematocrit fall. Severe PPH (WHO) = ≥1000 mL. (Book p528)

questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: Primary PPH occurs ______ and secondary PPH occurs ______.
opts: Within 24 h of delivery; >24 h to 12 weeks after delivery
questions.exp: Primary <24 h; secondary >24 h up to 12 weeks. (Book p528)

questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: Match the 4 Ts with the m/c examples – Tone : Trauma : Thrombin : Tissue.
opts: Atonic uterus (m/c overall & m/c 1° PPH) : perineal/cervical tear, hematoma, rupture : bleeding disorders : retained placental tissue (m/c 2° PPH)
Retained tissue : atonic uterus : tears : bleeding disorders
Bleeding disorders : retained tissue : atony : trauma
questions.exp: Tone – atonic uterus (m/c overall, m/c primary); Trauma – tears/hematoma/rupture; Thrombin – bleeding disorders; Tissue – retained placenta (m/c secondary). (Book p528)

questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: The 'living ligature' of the uterus refers to:
opts: The middle layer of myometrium whose fibres compress vessels on contraction; atony → no compression → PPH
questions.exp: Living ligature = middle layer of myometrium; muscle fibres compress vessels on contraction; atonic uterus → PPH. (Book p528)

questions.sec: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
questions.q: Postpartum dilatation and curettage carries the highest risk for ______; the best method to prevent PPH is ______.
opts: Asherman syndrome; active management of third stage of labour
questions.exp: Postpartum D&C → Asherman syndrome; best PPH prevention = AMTSL. (Book p528)

questions.sec: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
questions.q: Maternal risk factors for PPH include all EXCEPT:
opts: Previous history of PPH / advanced maternal age
H/O PIH in current pregnancy / anemia
questions.exp: Maternal: previous PPH, advanced age, obesity, multigravida, PIH in current pregnancy, anemia. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
questions.q: Placental risk factors for PPH are:
opts: Placenta previa, abruptio placentae (h/o APH), placenta accreta spectrum, chorioamnionitis
questions.exp: Placental: previa, abruption (H/O antepartum haemorrhage), PAS, chorioamnionitis. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
questions.q: Uterine risk factors relate to overdistension, e.g.:
opts: Twin pregnancy, gestational diabetes, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, fibroid uterus
questions.exp: Uterine overdistension: twins, GDM, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, fibroid. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
questions.q: Intrapartum risk factors for PPH include:
opts: Prolonged labour, precipitate labour (<3 h), induction/augmentation, instrumental delivery, overuse of tocolytics, general anaesthesia
questions.exp: Intrapartum: prolonged/precipitate labour, IOL/augmentation, instrumental delivery, tocolytic overuse, GA. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
questions.q: Specific risk factors for TRAUMATIC PPH:
opts: Instrumental delivery, breech extraction, obstructed labour, tachysystole (>5 contractions/10 min), ↑ parity & maternal age
questions.exp: Traumatic PPH: instrumental delivery, breech extraction, obstructed labour, tachysystole, multiparity and age. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Initial management: resuscitation & atonic vs traumatic PPH
questions.q: First step in managing PPH (an obstetric emergency requiring a synchronised approach) is resuscitation, which includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Large-bore IV cannula; blood samples for ABO/Rh, CBC, BT, CT; arrange blood
questions.exp: Resuscitation: IV cannula, blood samples, arrange blood, crystalloids 1000 mL/min, ABC, Foley catheter. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Initial management: resuscitation & atonic vs traumatic PPH
questions.q: After resuscitation, per-abdominal uterine massage finds a well-contracted uterus with normal tone. This:
opts: Rules out atonic PPH and indicates traumatic PPH → P/V examination to find the cause
questions.exp: Normal tone → atonic PPH ruled out → traumatic PPH → P/V examination. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Initial management: resuscitation & atonic vs traumatic PPH
questions.q: If uterine tone is ↓ and maintained only by massage, this indicates ______; the next step is ______.
opts: Atonic PPH; P/V examination to rule out retained membranes/placental parts (which can induce contractions), then atonic PPH management
questions.exp: ↓ tone = atonic PPH; P/V to rule out retained products, then manage atonic PPH. (Book p529)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: The three simultaneous steps in management of atonic PPH are:
opts: Bimanual uterine massage + injection tranexamic acid + uterotonic drug
questions.exp: Bimanual massage (one hand on abdomen, one in vagina) + TXA + uterotonic. (Book p530)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: Tranexamic acid in PPH – timing and dose:
opts: Within 3 h of PPH onset; 1 g in 100 mL NS IV over 20 min (fast rate → hypotension)
questions.exp: TXA within 3 h of onset; 1 g in 100 mL NS over 20 min; rapid infusion causes hypotension. (Book p530)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: Tranexamic acid dose is repeated if bleeding:
opts: Persists ≥30 min or reappears within 24 h
questions.exp: Repeat if bleeding persists ≥30 min or reappears within 24 h. (Book p530)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: Oxytocin in atonic PPH – WHO status, dose and cautions:
opts: First drug recommended by WHO; 20–40 IU IM/IV infusion; avoid IV bolus (hypotension, arrhythmia, MI, arrest); not in 5% dextrose
Second-line; 10 IU IV bolus; in dextrose
questions.exp: Oxytocin first (WHO); 20–40 IU IM/IV infusion; no IV bolus; avoid 5% dextrose (water intoxication). (Book p530)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: Natural vs synthetic oxytocin:
opts: Natural – nonapeptide from paraventricular nucleus of hypothalamus, stored in posterior pituitary, pulsatile release; synthetic – octapeptide stored at 2–8 °C
Natural – octapeptide from anterior pituitary; synthetic – nonapeptide at room temp
Natural – from supraoptic nucleus, stored in adrenal; synthetic – decapeptide
questions.exp: Natural: nonapeptide, paraventricular nucleus, posterior pituitary, pulsatile. Synthetic: octapeptide, 2–8 °C. (Book p530)

questions.sec: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
questions.q: Mechanism, half-life and kinetics of IM oxytocin:
opts: ↑ intracellular calcium and ↑ PGF2α from decidua; t½ 3–5 min; onset 3 min; duration 1 h; causes after-pains and milk ejection
↓ calcium; t½ 40 min; onset 10 min; duration 3 h
cAMP rise; t½ 1 h; onset 1 min; duration 30 min
Blocks progesterone; t½ 20 min; onset 5 min; duration 2 h
questions.exp: ↑ intracellular Ca2+, ↑ PGF2α release; t½ 3–5 min; IM onset 3 min, duration 1 h; after-pains and milk ejection. (Book p530)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Methylergometrine – effect and dose:
opts: Tetanic continuous contractions (cannot be used during pregnancy, may retain placenta); 0.2 mg IM repeated in 2–4 h; IV avoided (BP spike); brown vials (phototoxic)
Physiological contractions; 0.5 mg IV; clear vials
questions.exp: ME: tetanic contractions; 0.2 mg IM repeat 2–4 h; IV avoided; brown vials due to phototoxicity; S/E hypertension. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Contraindications to methylergometrine include all EXCEPT:
opts: After delivery of first twin / heart disease / peripheral vascular disease
Rh-negative pregnancy / HIV on protease inhibitors (relative)
questions.exp: Asthma is a C/I to carboprost, not ME. ME C/I: after 1st twin, heart disease, PVD, pre-eclampsia/HELLP, Rh-negative, HIV on PIs. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Syntometrine composition and note on carbetocin:
opts: 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg methylergometrine; expensive; carbetocin is used in AMTSL but not for PPH management
10 U oxytocin + 0.2 mg ME; cheap; carbetocin is PPH gold standard
questions.exp: Syntometrine = 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg ME (expensive, not readily available); carbetocin not for PPH treatment. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Misoprostol in PPH – form, WHO strategy and dose:
opts: PGE1, the only uterotonic in tablet form; WHO recommends antenatal distribution in rural areas; WHO 800 mcg sublingual > oral; ACOG 600–1000 mcg SL/oral/PR; PV avoided in PPH (washed off)
questions.exp: Misoprostol PGE1 tablet; WHO 800 mcg SL (> oral); ACOG 600–1000 mcg; avoid PV in PPH. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Side effects and contraindication of misoprostol:
opts: Hyperthermia & shivering, nausea & vomiting; C/I scarred uterus (m/c drug causing uterine rupture); safe in asthmatics
questions.exp: S/E: hyperthermia/shivering, nausea/vomiting; C/I scarred uterus (m/c drug causing rupture); can be given to asthmatics. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Carboprost (Hemabate) – class, status and dose:
opts: PGF2α; gold standard for PPH management; 250 mcg IM every 15–40 min, max 8 doses (2 mg); S/E diarrhoea
PGE2; first line; 500 mcg IV; S/E fever
PGE1; second line; 1 mg IM; S/E hypertension
questions.exp: Carboprost PGF2α – gold standard; 250 mcg IM q15–40 min, max 8 doses; S/E diarrhoea. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
questions.q: Contraindications to carboprost and the status of dinoprostone:
opts: Asthma, pulmonary hypertension, suspected amniotic fluid embolism, PIH (relative); dinoprostone (PGE2) used off-label PV/PR/suppository 20 mg, not WHO-recommended
Heart disease, Rh-negative; dinoprostone first line
questions.exp: Carboprost C/I: asthma, pulmonary HTN, suspected AFE, PIH (relative). Dinoprostone off-label 20 mg, not recommended by WHO. (Book p531)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: Sequence of uterotonics in the PPH management protocol:
opts: Bimanual massage + TXA + oxytocin → if unresponsive methylergometrine → if unresponsive carboprost; misoprostol is an add-on drug
questions.exp: Oxytocin (WHO first) → ME → carboprost; misoprostol as add-on. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: If unresponsive to drugs for >30 min, mechanical compression is used (continuing uterotonics) – principle and catheters:
opts: Warm NS in a catheter inside the uterus presses on venous sinuses; Bakri balloon (max 500 mL), Sengstaken-Blakemore, EBB uterine tamponade system, condom catheter
questions.exp: Balloon tamponade with warm NS compresses venous sinuses; Bakri (max 500 mL), SB tube, EBB system, condom catheter; vaginal balloon controls vaginal oozing. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: If tamponade is responsive, the catheter is removed after ______; if bleeding continues with unstable vitals the next step is ______.
questions.exp: Remove after 12–24 h if responsive; unstable vitals → uterine artery ligation. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: If bleeding continues but vitals are stable, the patient is shifted to OT with temporary measures such as:
opts: External aortic compression (at umbilicus, check ipsilateral femoral pulse) and military anti-shock garment
Vaginal packing and IV fluids only
questions.exp: Temporary measures: external aortic compression at umbilical level (absent femoral pulse confirms) and MAST. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: Compression sutures for PPH include (m/c first):
opts: B-Lynch/Brace (m/c), Hayman, Cho square, Pereira, Gunshella
questions.exp: B-Lynch (m/c), Hayman, Cho square, Pereira, Gunshella sutures. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: If bleeding continues after compression sutures – with radiointervention available : without radiointervention.
opts: Uterine artery embolization (if stable vitals) : stepwise devascularisation – unilateral UAL → bilateral UAL → unilateral ovarian anastomotic branch → bilateral ovarian branch ligation
questions.exp: Radiointervention → UAE; otherwise stepwise devascularisation: U/L UAL, B/L UAL, U/L then B/L ovarian anastomotic branch ligation. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
questions.q: Final steps if bleeding still continues – stable : unstable; and if hysterectomy fails to stop bleeding:
opts: Ligation of anterior division of internal iliac artery : subtotal hysterectomy (cervix not removed); pelvic pressure packs – umbrella pack, parachute pack
Total hysterectomy : internal iliac ligation; gauze pack
questions.exp: Stable → anterior division internal iliac ligation (if fails → hysterectomy); unstable → subtotal hysterectomy; persistent bleeding → umbrella/parachute pelvic packs. (Book p532)

questions.sec: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing
questions.q: Uterine artery ligation (O'Leary technique) is performed at:
opts: Site of upward turning of the artery in the broad ligament where the round ligament crosses; suture includes part of myometrium to prevent slipping; stay close to uterus to protect ureter
questions.exp: UAL at the upward turn in broad ligament where round ligament crosses; include myometrium; proximity to uterus protects ureter. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing
questions.q: Success rate of bilateral uterine artery ligation:
questions.exp: B/L UAL controls bleeding in ~85%. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing
questions.q: Shock index (SI) = heart rate ÷ systolic BP. Normal range and significance of SI ≥0.9:
opts: 0.5–0.7; ≥0.9 → blood transfusion indicated and ↑ risk of maternal mortality
questions.exp: Normal SI 0.5–0.7; SI ≥0.9 → transfuse, ↑ mortality risk. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing
questions.q: Packing of the uterus for PPH is:
questions.exp: Uterine packing is outdated; balloon tamponade is used instead. (Book p533)

questions.sec: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
questions.q: Features of the human placenta and the plane of separation:
opts: Deciduate, discoid, hemochorial; separates through zona spongiosa; most important factor = uterine contraction
questions.exp: Deciduate, discoid, hemochorial; uterine contraction is most important; plane = zona spongiosa. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
questions.q: Retained placenta (prolonged third stage) is defined as placenta not delivered:
questions.exp: Retained placenta = >30 min after delivery of baby. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
questions.q: Placenta separated but not expelled (signs of separation present) = trapped placenta. Management:
opts: Empty bladder → P/A exam; if uterus relaxed: oxytocin + CCT (if cord breaks → MRP under short GA); if uterus relaxed and internal os closed: MRP under short GA
questions.exp: Trapped placenta: empty bladder, oxytocin + CCT; if cord snaps or os closed → manual removal under short GA. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
questions.q: Placenta attached to uterus but not invading myometrium – management:
opts: Oxytocin + CCT; if no response → manual removal of placenta under GA
questions.exp: Adherent non-invasive: oxytocin + CCT → MRP under GA if no response. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
questions.q: Placenta invading the myometrium (morbidly adherent) is called ______ and managed by ______.
questions.exp: Morbidly adherent = placenta accreta spectrum → hysterectomy. (Book p534)

questions.sec: Placenta accreta spectrum
questions.q: Match PAS types by depth of chorionic villi – Accreta : Increta : Percreta.
opts: Superficially attached to myometrium (m/c) : invade into myometrium : attached to/through serosa
Into endometrium : into serosa : into bladder
questions.exp: Accreta (m/c) superficial attachment; increta invades myometrium; percreta reaches serosa. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Placenta accreta spectrum
questions.q: Risk factors and etiology of PAS:
opts: Placenta previa in current pregnancy; past C-section (most important), D&C, myomectomy; etiology – absent Nitabuch's layer / defective decidua basalis
questions.exp: Risk: previa now, prior C-section (most important), D&C, myomectomy. Etiology: absent Nitabuch's layer, defective decidua basalis. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Placenta accreta spectrum
questions.q: Investigation of choice for PAS and its findings:
opts: Ultrasound with Doppler – heterogenous/moth-eaten placenta with placental lakes, loss of hypoechoic area below placenta (absent decidua basalis), interrupted white line of bladder–serosa interface
questions.exp: USG + Doppler (IOC): moth-eaten placenta/lakes, loss of retroplacental hypoechoic zone, interrupted bladder-serosa line. Management: hysterectomy. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
questions.q: Uterine inversion is ______; on inspection the os is ______ in inversion and ______ in uterine prolapse.
opts: Prolapse of the fundus into the uterine cavity; not visible; visible
Descent of cervix through introitus; visible; not visible
Rupture of the fundus; visible; visible
Retroversion of uterus; not visible; not visible
questions.exp: Inversion = fundus prolapses into cavity; os not visible in inversion but visible in prolapse. (Book p535)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
questions.q: Classification by time after delivery – Acute : Sub-acute : Chronic.
questions.exp: Acute <24 h; sub-acute 24 h–4 wks; chronic ≥4 wks. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
questions.q: Classification by extent – 1st : 2nd : 3rd : 4th degree.
opts: Fundus into cavity not beyond os : fundus reaches os level, not protruding : fundus protrudes out of introitus : complete inversion of uterus and vagina
Fundus at os : fundus in vagina : fundus at introitus : vagina everted
Dimple in fundus : fundus at os : fundus in vagina : fundus outside
Fundus in vagina : at introitus : outside : with bladder
questions.exp: 1° within cavity; 2° reaches os; 3° protrudes out of introitus; 4° complete inversion of uterus and vagina. (Book p536)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
questions.q: The m/c cause of uterine inversion and the nature of shock:
opts: Iatrogenic (mismanaged 3rd stage); initial neurogenic shock (parasympathetic stretching) then hemorrhagic shock (cause of death)
questions.exp: M/c iatrogenic; shock immediately post-delivery – initially neurogenic, then hemorrhagic (cause of death). (Book p536)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
questions.q: Examination findings in uterine inversion – P/A : P/V; and the clinical clue:
opts: Cup-like depression below umbilicus or fundus not palpable : globular structure in vagina; shock immediately after birth out of proportion to blood loss
Hard contracted fundus : cervix visible; slow bleeding
Fundus above umbilicus : empty vagina; fever
Bandl's ring : bulging membranes; late shock
questions.exp: P/A cup-like depression/absent fundus; P/V globular mass; shock out of proportion to bleeding suggests inversion. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: management
questions.q: First steps in managing acute uterine inversion:
opts: Call for help + resuscitate → stop uterotonics (oxytocin) → manual replacement (Johnson's method)
Give oxytocin bolus → remove placenta → replace
questions.exp: Call for help, resuscitate, stop oxytocin, then Johnson's manual replacement. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: management
questions.q: Principles of Johnson's method:
opts: The part that prolapsed first is repositioned last; do NOT separate the placenta (↑ hemorrhage)
Remove placenta first, then replace fundus
questions.exp: First part to prolapse → last to be reposited; placenta not separated to avoid hemorrhage. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: management
questions.q: If Johnson's method fails, the sequence is:
opts: Repeat manual replacement under GA/uterine relaxant (terbutaline) → abdominal surgery (Huntington's / Haultain's method)
questions.exp: Repeat under GA/terbutaline → failing that, Huntington's or Haultain's abdominal surgery. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: management
questions.q: Match – Huntington's : Haultain's : outdated methods.
opts: Abdominal traction on the round ligaments/fundus : abdominal incision of the constriction ring : hydrostatic O'Sullivan, vaginal Spinelli and Kustner/Cascardi surgeries
questions.exp: Huntington's – abdominal replacement by traction; Haultain's – constriction ring incised; outdated: hydrostatic O'Sullivan, Spinelli and Cascardi vaginal surgeries. (Book p537)

questions.sec: Uterine inversion: management
questions.q: Post-replacement management (in order):
opts: Stop uterine relaxant → remove placenta → start oxytocin → start antibiotics
Start oxytocin → remove placenta → stop relaxant → antibiotics
questions.exp: 1 stop relaxant, 2 remove placenta, 3 start oxytocin, 4 antibiotics. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Amniotic fluid embolism (AFE) – alias and incidence:
opts: Anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy; 1 in 100,000 deliveries; catastrophic emergency
questions.exp: AFE = anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy, 1/100,000 deliveries. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Pathophysiology of AFE begins with ______ and the amniotic fluid (fetal skin cells, debris, antigens) produces three effects:
opts: Erratic uterine contractions → breach of maternal-fetal interface/open venous sinuses; pulmonary embolism symptoms (pathognomonic), factor VII & plasminogen activation → DIC, immunological reaction → SIRS
Hypotonic uterus; hemorrhage, sepsis, renal failure
questions.exp: Erratic contractions → breach → fluid enters circulation → pulmonary symptoms (pathognomonic), DIC, systemic inflammatory response. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Clinical phases of AFE – Phase I : Phase II.
opts: During labour/<30 min of delivery: respiratory depression + unexplained shock + minimal bleeding, breathlessness, SpO2 <60%, hypoxia & metabolic acidosis : DIC with excessive bleeding
questions.exp: Phase I respiratory depression, shock, minimal bleeding, SpO2 <60%; Phase II DIC → excessive bleeding. (Book p538)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Clinical criteria for AFE diagnosis include all EXCEPT:
opts: Unexplained shock with minimal bleeding / onset within 30 min of labour
questions.exp: Criteria: unexplained shock, onset within 30 min, breathlessness/shock, overt DIC, NO fever; also pulmonary vessel catheterisation. Management is ICU care; ↑ mortality. (Book p539)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Postpartum collapse – time of appearance: PPH : uterine inversion : AFE.
opts: Within 24 h : within 24 h : within 30 min of delivery
Within 30 min : within 24 h : within 1 wk
Within 1 h : within 30 min : within 24 h
questions.exp: PPH and inversion within 24 h; AFE within 30 min. (Book p539)

questions.sec: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
questions.q: Postpartum collapse examination – P/A and P/V findings: PPH : uterine inversion : AFE.
opts: ↓ tone, ↑ blood loss : cup-like depression below umbilicus, globular mass in vagina : normal, normal
questions.exp: PPH: ↓ tone/↑ bleeding (m/c cause of collapse); inversion: cup depression/globular vaginal mass with shock + minimal bleeding; AFE: normal P/A and P/V. (Book p539)

units.title: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts
units.guide: Pin down every PPH definition (volume, ACOG, clinical, WHO severe), the primary/secondary split, and the 4 T causes with their m/c examples. Focus for this checkpoint: PPH: definitions, types & the 4 Ts.

units.title: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH
units.guide: Sort the maternal, placental, uterine and intrapartum risk factors, and recall the five specific risks for traumatic PPH. Focus for this checkpoint: Risk factors for atonic & traumatic PPH.

units.title: Initial management: resuscitation & atonic vs traumatic PPH
units.guide: Run the six-point resuscitation, then use per-abdominal massage to split atonic from traumatic PPH and decide the next examination. Focus for this checkpoint: Initial management: resuscitation & atonic vs traumatic PPH.

units.title: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid
units.guide: Perform bimanual massage, give tranexamic acid at the right dose and timing, and start the WHO first-choice uterotonic. Focus for this checkpoint: Atonic PPH: three simultaneous steps & tranexamic acid.

units.title: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost
units.guide: Dose each second-line drug, identify its unique contraindications and side effects, and know which is the gold standard. Focus for this checkpoint: Second-line uterotonics: methylergometrine, syntometrine, misoprostol & carboprost.

units.title: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery
units.guide: Follow the escalation ladder from first-line uterotonics through balloon tamponade, compression sutures, devascularisation and hysterectomy. Focus for this checkpoint: Management protocol: drugs → balloon tamponade → surgery.

units.title: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing
units.guide: Place the O'Leary suture correctly, quote its success rate, compute the shock index and remember which old method is obsolete. Focus for this checkpoint: Uterine artery ligation, shock index & packing.

units.title: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm
units.guide: Define retained placenta and manage each of its three causes – trapped, adherent-non-invasive and morbidly adherent. Focus for this checkpoint: Retained placenta: causes & management algorithm.

units.title: Placenta accreta spectrum
units.guide: Grade accreta, increta and percreta by depth, know the risk factors, etiology, Doppler signs and definitive treatment. Focus for this checkpoint: Placenta accreta spectrum.

units.title: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features
units.guide: Distinguish inversion from prolapse, classify by time and degree, and recognise the neurogenic-then-hemorrhagic shock picture. Focus for this checkpoint: Uterine inversion: definition, classification & clinical features.

units.title: Uterine inversion: management
units.guide: Apply Johnson's manual replacement principles, know the surgical fall-backs and outdated methods, and the four post-replacement steps. Focus for this checkpoint: Uterine inversion: management.

units.title: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse
units.guide: Explain AFE pathophysiology and its two clinical phases, the clinical diagnostic criteria, and differentiate the three causes of postpartum collapse. Focus for this checkpoint: Amniotic fluid embolism & postpartum collapse.
